svg.text: blue = rows · yellow = columns · diode band → row · same holes on both halves
Right half trackball: SCLK 008, SDIO 011, NCS 100, MOTION 006, plus VCC + GND. Positions from cosmos-41.kls.json (2D layout, not the curved case).
One key, close up (seen from below)
Yellow and blue never touch each other directly: the switch connects them only while the key is pressed.
Trick: diode legs as the row wire
band legs bent sideways and soldered to each other
bent band legs = the row → blue wire only to the controller
(use blue between keys where the legs can't reach)
Close-up: how one key connects (q w e / a s d, seen from below)
switch pin → diode → band end → BLUE row wire · other switch pin → YELLOW column wire
● grey dots = solder joints · black band always on the row side · one row wire can touch many band legs
Rows and columns never touch metal-to-metal; crossing over insulated wire is fine.
Full wiring: every key, diode and wire (top view, as if the case were see-through)
Each diode lies sideways from pin 2 toward the next key in its row (blue = row wire).
Case upside down for soldering = the next picture (mirrored). Grey dots = solder joints. Turquoise holes = trackball (right board).
Dashed line = the wire from the end of that row/column to its hole. Controller position is schematic: route to wherever the holder sits, with ~3 cm slack.
SOLDERING VIEW: each half flipped over (what you see with the case upside down)
Left↔right mirrored vs. the top view; labels kept readable. Outer pinky column is now on the inside edge.
Board drawn from its back (hole rows swap sides). If you see the chip, read the holes from the top view.
Dashed line = the wire from the end of that row/column to its hole. Controller position is schematic: route to wherever the holder sits, with ~3 cm slack.
SOLDERING VIEW + DIODE-LEG ROWS: each colour = one diode; colour changes where it's soldered to the next
Left↔right mirrored vs. the top view; labels kept readable. Outer pinky column is now on the inside edge.
Board drawn from its back (hole rows swap sides). If you see the chip, read the holes from the top view.
Dashed line = the wire from the end of that row/column to its hole. Controller position is schematic: route to wherever the holder sits, with ~3 cm slack.
